title: Avesta — Vendidad
dateDisplay: c. 1st millennium BCE; written down in the Sasanian period
attributionNote: The Vendidad is an anonymous priestly compilation. It is traditionally ascribed to Zarathushtra's revelation but was assembled long after the Gathas; the surviving Avestan text is a fragment of a larger collection.
description: The Vendidad, the only complete book of the Avesta, in twenty-two fargards. It opens with the creation of sixteen lands by Ahura Mazda and their counter-creations, and then sets out the purity law of the community: the treatment of corpses and the dead, the cleansing of pollution, the care of dogs and fires, contracts and assaults, and the ritual that restores a person to the sacred order.
historicalContext: The Vendidad was transmitted with the Yasna in the Zoroastrian liturgy and was written down in the Sasanian period from much older material. James Darmesteter's translation was published in the Sacred Books of the East, volume 4 (1880), with an introduction that founded the modern study of the text.
availabilityNote: Complete. All twenty-two fargards of Darmesteter's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one fargard per chapter. The volume's introduction is not part of the work; the translator's footnotes printed on each fargard page are kept.
